transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-14
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Sam Okoro (AuroraX CTO), Jamie Chen (AuroraX ML Eng), Dana Ruiz (AuroraX Infra Lead), Liam Park (AuroraX PM)

Auto-summary (auto gen):
AuroraX is evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private for a multilingual legal-document assistant with 250k token/day throughput, occasional 100k-token context windows, and tool-calling to internal document store and billing tools. Key concerns: latency, cost, data residency, SSO/KMS, and model quality for legal domain. Next steps: share perf/cost matrix, pilot setup, security docs.

Topics:
- Model choices (Llama-3 variants, Mistral, MosaicML, RedPajama, Llama 2 fine-tuned legal models)
- Context length & long prompts (100k token windows, local retrieval vs context)
- Multilingual support (EN, FR, ES, DE) and hallucination risk
- Tool-calling (internal doc search, DB lookups, billing system)
- Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Security & compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everybody, thanks for carving time today, appreciate it. Quick roll call? I'll let folks say hi.
[00:08] Sam (AuroraX CTO): Hey Alex, Sam here. Excited to dig in, we have Jamie, Dana, Liam on as well.
[00:14] Jamie (AuroraX ML Eng): Jamie, hi. Looking for a plan that supports very long context for contracts and also multilingual answers.
[00:21] Dana (AuroraX Infra): Dana, infra. We'll be owning the pilot infra if we go dedicated or private.
[00:26] Liam (AuroraX PM): Liam here, I'll own success criteria and timelines.
[00:30] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi everyone, Priya from Redwood, I'll focus on performance and ops questions.

[00:40] Alex: Cool. Agenda — quick context from AuroraX, then model options and tradeoffs, deployment modes, tool-calling pattern, security checklist, and then concrete next steps. Sam, do you want to kick off with the highest-level goals?
[00:53] Sam: Yeah. We're building a legal assistant that ingests contracts and produces clause summaries, risk flags, and suggested redlines. It's across EN/FR/ES/DE. Main non-functional: latency under 2s for short queries, but we also need the ability to pass extremely long contexts — sometimes a user wants a 70k token contract in full. Throughput estimate roughly 250k tokens/day, peak concurrent 40 sessions. Also strict data residency for EU customers, and auditability.
[01:30] Alex: Good. So two axes: long-context capabilities and multilingual robustness. Quick question on hallucination tolerance — are low hallucinations mandatory for legal outputs?
[01:42] Liam: Yes, low hallucination is critical. We need attribution to source sections where possible and the ability to run deterministic reranks against the doc-store.

[01:55] Priya: Great. On model choices, we typically recommend a small set to evaluate: Llama-3 8B/16B variants (we've got Redwood-verified profiles), Mistral open weights, Mosaic XL like families, and some specialized fine-tuned legal models like RP-legal (redpajama derivations) or vendor fine-tunes. For very long context, model architecture matters — transformer variants with efficient KV handling and chunking + retrieval are key.
[02:25] Jamie: We were thinking about forcing everything into retrieval augmentation instead of single huge context; but sometimes the user wants a full contract as context for line-by-line edits.
[02:36] Priya: Right, and that shapes the infra: if you need a 70–100k token live context, we can either route to models with extended context (some Llama 3 variants support 64k natively, some extended tokens setups go to 128k with segmentation), or use KV cache + streaming and intelligent local chunking. There are trade-offs: extended-context model variants increase latency and memory per-request and cost per token; retrieval+reconstruction reduces memory but adds retrieval latency and potential coherence issues.

[03:10] Sam: Can you quantify cost delta between hosted and dedicated when running an extended-context model? ballpark is fine.
[03:18] Alex: Ballpark — for our hosted tier, extended-context Llama-3-16k/32k-style variants cost ~3–4x per token compared to base short-context models because of GPU memory and slower throughput. Dedicated reserved capacity, with optimized quantization and batching, can cut that in half or more depending on utilization. For private on-prem, cost is very customer dependent — CapEx but lower per-token runtime costs if you amortize GPUs.
[03:46] Dana: On-prem raises our compliance flag—some of our EU customers require data never leave region. Redwood Private with a VPC control plane is interesting if you can keep inference in our cloud region.
[03:57] Alex: Yes, Redwood Private supports region-bounded deployments and customer-managed KMS; we've done VPC-only control planes with HSM integrations for a handful of customers.

[04:08] Jamie: On multilingual — are there models you recommend that handle EN/FR/ES/DE equally well? We're worried about quality variance.
[04:15] Priya: In general, multilingual performance correlates with pretraining data; open models like Mistral are strong in English, mixed elsewhere. Llama 3 tends to have better cross-lingual behavior with the larger parameter sizes. We also recommend fine-tuning or mixing in synthetic bilingual fine-tuning on legal corpora. Another approach is language-specific reranker + translation fallback for lower-resource languages.
[04:43] Sam: Are there Redwood features to manage model family per-region? e.g., route EU requests to a model variant that complies with residency or fine-tunes?
[04:52] Alex: Yes, smart routing can pin by region or tier. You can define policies: EU traffic → dedicated EU pool running private-licensed model, default global → hosted. We also support automatic fallback to cheaper or short-context variants when capacity is constrained.

[05:08] Liam: Tool-calling — we need safe, auditable tool calls to our search/index and billing. How do you do authentication and least privilege for tool integrations?
[05:18] Priya: Tool-calls can be proxied via Redwood's tool gateway or direct. For enterprise pilots we recommend the gateway with short-lived credentials, per-tool RBAC, and audit logs. We can integrate with your SAML/SSO so calls are traced to user identities. Also recommended: canonical verifier service on your side that checks tool output.
[05:40] Dana: So for security, we need SOC2 docs, SAML, per-token encryption, and KMS integration. Do you support customer-managed keys?
[05:50] Alex: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for Private deployments, and for Dedicated we can integrate KMS/HSM as part of the appliance. Hosted supports encryption at rest and in transit; CMK is an enterprise add-on.

[06:05] Jamie: On the topic of evals — we need to run a regression suite for hallucination and legal accuracy. Does Redwood provide eval harnesses or can we plug in our own?
[06:14] Priya: We have Redwood Optimize — it suggests model/quantization recommendations and supports eval integrations. You can upload labeled prompt sets and we'll run continuous evals and differential alerts when new model versions degrade.
[06:28] Sam: Good. About performance — we want sub-2s p95 for short queries. Is that realistic with tool-calling and attribution?
[06:37] Priya: Short queries without large context and without external tool calls are usually sub-500ms p95 on hosted for lightweight models. With attribution and tool calls you're adding network/RPC latency. For sub-2s you should rely on colocated dedicated pools and caching for common docs — prefix/KV caching helps a lot. We'll show config examples.

[07:02] Speaker 1: (mumble) How about streaming vs non-streaming? We need the UI to update as the model composes.
[07:10] Alex: Streaming supported across Hosted and Dedicated; Private deploys have streaming support depending on your network setup. For long context, streaming plus incremental KV flush reduces perceived latency.

[07:22] Jamie: Any special notes about quantization and legal accuracy? We worry that heavy quantization reduces answer fidelity.
[07:28] Priya: True — 4-bit quantization offers great cost savings but can slightly increase error rates, especially for fine-grained factual legal citations. We recommend a mixed approach: keep higher-precision for reranker or critic models and lower precision for bulk generation. Redwood Optimize can recommend which model layers to quantize and give expected delta.

[07:50] Liam: Timeline and success criteria — we want a pilot in 3–4 weeks to validate viability and costs, then production in Q2. Success criteria: p95 latency <2s for short queries, reliable 70k-context handling without OOMs, hallucination <2% on benchmark, and regional residency for EU traffic.
[08:10] Alex: That's achievable as a pilot. Our typical pilot looks like: 2-week perf baseline with a 1–2 GPU dedicated pool or hosted baseline, then 2-week extended-context validation. For on-prem, schedule is longer due to procurement.

[08:25] Sam: What's an example config for the extended context? like memory, batch sizes, caching.
[08:32] Priya: Example: for a 70k token context on a 16B extension model, common config is to use 80–90GB GPU memory per replica (A100-class), batch concurrency 4–8 depending on latency SLO, and prefix KV caching for repeated doc access. We use continuous batching but with priority lanes for low-latency calls. We can share a sample config.

[09:00] Dana: If we go Dedicated, how do rollouts work? We have multiple teams using different models.
[09:07] Alex: Rolling deploys: Redwood Console supports canary/A-B rollouts, pinning model versions per-route, and auto-fallback if error budgets exceed thresholds. We can enforce per-team quotas and isolation.

[09:24] Jamie: Are there any red flags for us if we push to Private on-prem? Network egress, license for models, support SLAs?
[09:31] Priya: Biggest friction points: hardware procurement and networking (NAT, peering), model licensing for certain commercial models, and initial integrations for monitoring. We do offer a deployment checklist and a runbook.

[09:48] Sam: Competitors — we've talked to vendors who offer managed endpoints but not the routing or ops that you describe. We're assessing cost and lock-in risk.
[09:56] Alex: Understood. We emphasize portability so you can move models between hosted and private with the same config. We also provide model export hooks for audit.

[10:08] Liam: Ok let's recap and next steps.
[10:12] Alex: Recap: we'll send a model-performance + cost matrix, a sample config for 70k token context, security docs (SOC2, architecture for VPC and CMK), and suggested pilot plan. Action items we'll capture.

[10:28] Jamie: One more question — does Redwood support tool-calls that are synchronous vs asynchronous? We have background workers too.
[10:36] Priya: Both. Synchronous tool calls for immediate lookups + async callbacks/webhooks for longer-running ops. You can configure retries, idempotency keys, and audit logs.

[10:50] Dana: For the pilot region, we want EU-only for the EU customer cohort. Can Redwood guarantee region isolation for Dedicated in our requested cloud region?
[10:59] Alex: Yes, dedicated EU pools can be pinned to region; private VPC can be deployed in your specified region as well. We'll include region-bound deployment notes in the docs.

[11:12] Sam: Alright thanks. If you could prioritize the perf matrix and a clear hosted vs dedicated TCO that would help.
[11:20] Alex: We'll do that. Priya, anything to add before we close?
[11:24] Priya: I'll include a sample test harness and recommended eval prompts for legal domain. Also a note on mixing quantization levels per model.

[11:34] Alex: Perfect. We'll follow up with calendar invite for the pilot kickoff and send the docs. Thanks everyone.
[11:40] Sam: Thanks all.
